title: The doctor
description: Name the words for illness, and say what you need.
grammar: tener and a noun, and gender and articles
grammarNote: You already know cómo estás: the words for how you feel are nouns, and tener says you have them.

explanation.summary: Illness in Spanish is mostly a noun you have: tienes una tos, tienes fiebre, tienes dolor. The words for medicine and appointments are ordinary nouns around it.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La medicina, la cita, la pastilla, la tos, la herida, la piel y la vacuna are feminine. El hueso, el estómago y el antibiótico are masculine. El antibiótico is one you will hear a lot, and it is masculine even though it ends in -o.

sections.heading: What you have
sections.body: You know tener, and the words for illness go straight after it: tengo una tos, tienes una herida, tiene dolor de cabeza. Estar says how you are: la piel está roja, the skin is red.

examples.es: la herida está en la pierna
examples.en: the wound is on the leg

items.note: Masculine: el hueso. The plural is los huesos.
Masculine: el estómago. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el antibiótico. The accent marks the stress.

drills.note: Tos is feminine, so una tos.

drills.meaning: I need a tablet and an appointment
drills.note: Cita is feminine, so una cita.
